summary: Bank-fee approval slice: BankCharge gains the approval chain (submitted_by/at, approved_by/at, reject_reason) through a costing migration 0004 whose trigger replaces the PH-244 draft-only guard with draft-edit/submit/decide transitions that freeze published facts and keep BankCharge.version unchanged except for draft revisions. The costing service adds submit (draft->pending, records submitter) and independent decide (pending->approved/rejected, records approver and mandatory rejection reason; creator/submitter cannot decide), with company lock, period/lock/future checks, per-action BankChargeReceipt idempotency (same token replay without new writes, changed input conflict) and one-winner semantics. Approval posts exactly one company cost fact set in the same transaction: one SourceConsumption claim (consumer=cost, coverage_key=bank_charge:<id>, amount=gross, source=bank_charge ref), one core AccountingEvent (event_type=costing.bank_charge.cost, frozen occurred_on/posting_period, effect=gross) and one LedgerPosting (book=cost, origin=current, scope=project, amount=gross), with generic audits submitted/approved/rejected/cost_posted and no new canonical topic (per spec; saved event stays only on the save path). core.services.decide_document implements the core.document.decide bank_charge handler (private service/browser workflow, command channel not exposed). Views/forms/templates add submit, independent approve and reject plus approval-chain/cost display. verify_integrity now accepts the five statuses, validates the approval chain, requires no cost facts for unapproved states and validates exactly one complete cost fact set when present for approved charges (PH-253-compatible transitional allowance when absent), with orphan cost-event/stray-claim detection and labor-loop allowlisting of the fee cost event. No cash fact, ledger cash/bank posting, settlement/open-item or ReceiptFeeSettlement write is made.
